artworks.title: The Ludovisi Ares
artworks.description: A Roman marble statue of Ares seated at rest, his weapons set aside and a small Eros playing at his feet — the god of war momentarily disarmed by love. Restored by Gian Lorenzo Bernini in 1622, it is displayed in the Palazzo Altemps, Rome.

artworks.title: Venus and Mars
artworks.description: A Renaissance panel painting showing Mars sunk in deep sleep while a watchful Venus reclines opposite and infant satyrs make sport with his lance and armor. An allegory of love disarming war, it hangs in the National Gallery, London.

artworks.title: The Consequences of War
artworks.description: A Baroque oil painting in which Mars is dragged toward destruction by the Fury Alecto while Venus vainly tries to hold him back. Painted during the Thirty Years' War as an allegory of a Europe ravaged by conflict, it is held in the Palazzo Pitti, Florence.

films.title: Wonder Woman
films.description: Jenkins' origin film makes Ares the war behind the War — the god of conflict as the secret architect of the twentieth century's slaughter, and Diana's true opponent.

films.title: Xena: Warrior Princess
films.description: Kevin Smith's Ares is the series' recurring dark flirtation: the god of war as leather-clad tempter, ally and adversary across six seasons of syndicated myth.

films.title: Immortals
films.description: Tarsem's bronze-and-blood Olympus puts Ares in the melee against the Titans — war incarnate in a fight staged like a living frieze.

films.title: Hercules: The Legendary Journeys
films.description: Kevin Smith's Ares crosses over from Xena into the Renaissance Pictures Hercules cycle — the god of war as recurring half-brother, tempter and antagonist across the shared Olympus.

films.title: Blood of Zeus
films.description: Netflix's adult myth cycle keeps Ares among the Olympians at war — the god of conflict as a brutal player in the gods' civil bloodletting.

popCulture.title: God of War
popCulture.creator: Santa Monica Studio
popCulture.description: The game that named a franchise: Kratos begins as Ares' pawn and ends as his killer, seizing the title God of War from the Olympian who forged him.

popCulture.title: Hades
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Ares' boons are doom and blade — the god of war as a red-mist build, urging Zagreus to keep the blood flowing.

popCulture.title: Hades II
popCulture.creator: Supergiant Games
popCulture.description: Ares returns among the Olympian boon-givers — still the god of blade and bloodshed, now arming Melinoë's war on Chronos.

popCulture.title: Ares (DC Comics)
popCulture.creator: DC Comics
popCulture.description: Wonder Woman's Olympian nemesis across decades of comics — Ares as the immortal war-monger whose schemes keep Diana's lasso busy.

popCulture.title: Percy Jackson & the Olympians
popCulture.creator: Rick Riordan
popCulture.description: Riordan's demigod saga makes Ares a leather-jacketed bully god — father of Clarisse, adversary of Percy, and the war god as American roadside menace.

music.title: The Planets — Mars, the Bringer of War
music.description: Holst's opening movement makes the Roman Mars — Ares under another name — a colossal war-machine in 5/4: the planetary suite's most famous face of battle.

music.title: The Loves of Mars and Venus
music.description: Weaver's Drury Lane ballet stages Mars' affair with Venus and Vulcan's revenge — the war god caught in the forge-net, danced as England's first modern narrative ballet.

music.title: EPIC: The Musical
music.description: Rivera-Herrans' Odyssey concept album puts Ares in the 'God Games' gauntlet — the war god as one of Athena's divine opponents in a sung Olympus tribunal.
